    CHAPTER I

“He came at nine a.m. and left again before noon,” she told them.

The train was due at four a. m. but did not arrive until seven.

He said 'nothing at all' about the matter to anybody in the house.

She said ‘nothing at all’ about it either, which was stranger yet.

He wrote "a long letter" to his brother in the north that evening.

He wrote “a second letter” to his sister on the following morning.

They set out today for the coast, meaning to be back by Saturday.

They had gone to-day rather than wait upon the weather any longer.

The wind came out of the northeast and blew steadily all night.

A gale from the north-east had wrecked two boats the year before.

Then Mr. Fenton called upon Mrs. Fenton at the house by the church.

But Mr Fenton had not been seen in the village since the spring.

The name M’Gregor was carved above the door of the little shop.

The name M‘Gregor appeared in the parish register of that year.

The compositor set this line twice by mistake in the second proof.
The compositor set this line twice by mistake in the second proof.
